name: Double Outlet Right Ventricle with Subaortic Ventricular Septal Defect
aliases: Double outlet right ventricle, subaortic type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Heart Disease Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Both great arteries arise predominantly from the right ventricle
Presence of a subaortic ventricular septal defect allowing left ventricular outflow
Echocardiographic visualization of abnormal ventricular-arterial connections and VSD
Signs of cyanotic congenital heart disease in neonates or infants

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both great arteries arising from the right ventricle with a subaortic VSD confirmed by echocardiography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Cardiac MRI and catheterization may aid in detailed anatomical assessment

pathognomonic.notes: Bluish discoloration of lips and mucous membranes due to hypoxemia

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic murmur due to VSD and outflow tract obstruction
pathognomonic.notes: Harsh murmur best heard at left lower sternal border
searchTerms: murmur due to hole in heart

common.notes: Rapid breathing due to pulmonary overcirculation or heart failure
Secondary to increased metabolic demand and heart failure
Inadequate weight gain due to chronic hypoxia and cardiac workload

occasional.notes: Shortness of breath during feeding or activity
Enlarged liver due to right heart failure
Sympathetic activation due to cardiac stress

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to paradoxical embolism
rare.notes: Stroke or transient ischemic attacks secondary to right-to-left shunting
searchTerms: brain deficits due to abnormal blood clots

rare.notes: Elevated pulmonary artery pressures from increased flow
Infective endocarditis on abnormal cardiac structures

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit due to secondary polycythemia
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating both great arteries arising from right ventricle and subaortic VSD
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical delineation
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with chromosomal anomalies such as 22q11 deletion syndrome
other: Cardiac catheterization to assess hemodynamics and pulmonary pressures

distinguishingFeatures: Overriding aorta rather than both great arteries arising from right ventricle
Pulmonary stenosis with right ventricular hypertrophy
Aorta arises from right ventricle and pulmonary artery from left ventricle
No ventricular septal defect in some cases
Parallel rather than side-by-side great arteries

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties
references: Anderson RH, et al. Double outlet right ventricle: anatomical and clinical considerations. Heart. 2014;100(7):544-552.
Moller JH, et al. The clinical spectrum of double outlet right ventricle. Circulation. 2000;102(19):2345-2350.
Orphanet: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect (ORPHA:99044)
